Question: Down deep to your heart, do you believe that there's heaven?
Answer: I believe in a creator God. What that really means, I have no idea. I like to think he’s a big clockmaker and the purpose of the universe is to tell the time. Bad things happen because if you interrupt them it would be like interrupting a gear on a clock and it wouldn’t tell the right time anymore. Perhaps there is a great purpose to the movement of the universe in this clock-like motion. I don’t know. The problem with “heaven” is that it’s an undefined and undefinable word. What is heaven? Is it a place? A state of consciousness? A part of the creator? Where is it? When is it? I have no idea and not enough imagination to even try to create it. When I was a child I used to think that even if heaven was everything I wanted that eventually I would get bored doing all the things I loved to do and getting everything I wanted. It could not possibly be that way, the way my childhood mind envisioned it. And based on the Bible itself, Heaven can’t be “all that” because the Devil fights against it and runs away from it. It must be much like Earth with greed and ambition and disappointment and betrayal because otherwise why would Satan ever want to fight against God or leave “paradise”? At one point, a friend experienced a near-death event where he described heaven as being part of God, as being pure love, working towards a purpose for God and that time had no meaning and that there was no chance for boredom or distraction because you didn’t want to do anything but focus on the achievement of God’s plan, not because you were brainwashed or forced but because you WANTED to do it. At the time, I was drifting from belief - and to be sure I still have some serious doubts about any of it - but it really did fill in the gaps for me and it helped re-ignite my belief in a creator and a life after death. I can’t tell you what it’s like to climb Mt Everest, the grueling conditions, the cold, the burning lungs from lack of oxygen, the fear of a false step - I have never been there - but I know it exists and I know it’s hard to get up there. I can’t tell you about heaven because I have no frame of reference. No one has ever come back to tell me what it’s like, but there have been a few notable almost-supernatural events where my dead mother apparently left messages for me not to worry. Probably all bullshit. Maybe not. I don’t know. In the movie “War of the Worlds” with Gene Barry, he says of the aliens, “If they are mortal they must have mortal weaknesses.” and just because I as a weak, stupid human can’t understand the concept of heaven, it’s because, as Jesus said, “I think like a man thinks, not as God thinks.”. That’s okay. I don’t have to know what it is - I just have to believe it exists. It gives me comfort to believe that maybe someday, somewhere, there is something better than this place.
